description: Four-panel composite figure of EBSD impact-fracture cross-sections combining orientation/grain-boundary maps with kernel average misorientation (KAM) maps. (a) and (c) are BC + IPF + GB maps (10 µm scale bars) of the 0Al and 1.3Al steels respectively; each carries a yellow rectangle whose region is reproduced as a magnified inset in the upper-right corner. In both maps the fracture surface is the black/grey band along the lower edge, visible as grey or white (unindexed) areas at the top of both insets. (b) and (d) are the corresponding KAM maps (10 µm scale bars), with a black dashed line tracing the main crack path in (b); both share a 0°–3.5° colour bar (blue → red) whose legend lists the fraction of each class. The 0Al steel (b) shows red/yellow high-KAM patches adjacent to the crack with large blue undeformed matrix areas, average KAM 1.16°; the 1.3Al steel (d) is uniformly green with average KAM 1.31°. The figure demonstrates that transgranular crack paths deflect at block boundaries, and that NiAl clusters in 1.3Al homogenize the strain distribution near the fracture surface.

observations.observation: The figure contains four panels: (a, c) are BC + IPF + GB EBSD maps and (b, d) are the corresponding KAM maps, each with a 10 µm scale bar.
Panels (a) and (c) each contain a yellow rectangle whose contents are enlarged in a corner inset, and (b, d) are stated to be magnified views of those marked regions of (a, c) respectively.
The fracture surface appears as a dark/black band along the lower part of (a) and (b), with the crack path in (b) highlighted by a black dashed line.
The KAM colour bar in (b) and (d) spans 0° to 3.5°, with higher values conventionally indicating larger local strain.
Printed average KAM values are 1.16 for the 0Al steel (b) and 1.31 for the 1.3Al steel (d).
The caption states the average KAM of the 0Al steel is 1.16° and of the 1.3Al steel is 1.31°, matching the numbers printed on panels (b) and (d).

In (b) the region around the main crack is dominated by red and yellow (high-KAM) areas while adjacent matrix areas are blue (undeformed), indicating an inhomogeneous strain distribution in the 0Al steel.
Panel (d) shows a relatively uniform green KAM field across both the fracture surface and the surrounding matrix of the 1.3Al steel, indicating a more homogeneous strain distribution.
Panel (d) retains a smaller fraction (15.0%) of the lowest 0.0-0.7° KAM class than panel (b) (23.8%), consistent with the visible absence of large blue undeformed areas in the 1.3Al steel.

The citing text states that prior austenite grain boundaries (15° ≤ θ < 50°) are drawn in yellow and packet or block boundaries (θ ≥ 50°) in blue in the (a, c) maps, and that cracks propagate transgranularly, deflecting at block boundaries.

The citing text reports dislocation densities of ~2.20 × 10^15 m^-2 for the 1.3Al steel versus ~2.01 × 10^15 m^-2 for the 0Al steel, and states that the matrix KAM of the 1.3Al steel away from the crack is 0.79 (Fig. S5), rising to 1.31 near the fracture surface — none of which is shown in these panels.

subfigures.description: BC + IPF + GB orientation map of the 0Al steel impact-fracture cross-section, 10 µm scale bar, with a yellow-boxed region shown magnified in the top-right inset; the black/dark band at the bottom is the fracture surface, and cracks step across multicoloured packets/grains. Legend colours for boundary types are not visible in this panel.

KAM map of the 0Al steel (10 µm scale bar) with a black dashed line marking the main crack path; matrix is largely blue/green (low KAM) with red/yellow bands adjacent to the crack. Colour bar 0°–3.5°; legend: 0.0-0.7° 23.8%, 0.7-1.4° 47.5%, 1.4-2.1° 19.8%, 2.1-2.8° 6.5%, 2.8-3.5° 2.4%. Printed average KAM value 1.16.

BC + IPF + GB orientation map of the 1.3Al steel impact-fracture cross-section, 10 µm scale bar, with a large dark grey crack / fracture region running through the centre and a yellow-boxed region magnified as the right-hand inset; the surrounding matrix consists of fine multicoloured packets and blocks.

KAM map of the 1.3Al steel (10 µm scale bar) showing a visually uniform green field with only scattered yellow/red points; white gaps on the left and lower-left are unindexed/absent material. Colour bar 0°–3.5°; legend: 0.0-0.7° 15.0%, 0.7-1.4° 48.2%, 1.4-2.1° 25.9%, 2.1-2.8° 8.4%, 2.8-3.5° 2.6%. Printed average KAM value 1.31.

unreadable_items: panel (b): the blue legend row (0.0-0.7°, 23.8%) is partially overlapped by the 10 µm scale bar, though still readable
panel (a) and (c): the colour keys for IPF orientations and for the yellow/blue boundary types (15° ≤ θ < 50° and θ ≥ 50°) are described only in the citing text and are not printed inside the panels
